findings.issue: ClockGuard.StartAsync (line 157) creates a TimeProvider timer whose callback calls IClockCheckService.CheckAsync, which does db.ClockChecks.Add(...) + SaveChangesAsync on the injected WakeelDb; ReminderScheduler.Start/RunOnceAsync does the same every minute (reads six tables, writes notifications). Both services are registered Scoped (ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs lines 58-62) and resolve WakeelDb from the scope, but the host has exactly ONE WakeelDb: the singleton AccountSession holds one DbSession and exposes AccountSession.Db (src/Wakeel.UI/Services/Account/AccountSession.cs:74), so every scope hands out the same DbContext the Blazor UI is already using. EF Core's DbContext is not thread-safe. The moment the shell calls IClockGuard.StartAsync or IReminderScheduler.Start as the interfaces instruct, a background pass that overlaps any UI query throws 'A second operation was started on this context instance before a previous operation completed' (or corrupts the change tracker). Worse, both timer callbacks swallow every exception, so the ten-minute clock re-check and the minute reminder pass would fail permanently and silently while the UI shows «حدث خطأ غير متوقع» to the user. Nothing in either interface's XML doc warns the caller.
findings.fix: Stop using the ambient scoped WakeelDb from a timer callback. Either (a) inject IServiceScopeFactory into ClockGuard and ReminderScheduler and open a fresh scope (with its own WakeelDb over its own SqliteConnection) inside each timer callback, disposing it at the end of the pass; or (b) if the single encrypted connection must be kept, put a SemaphoreSlim inside DbSession, expose it, and have RunOnceAsync and ClockGuard's interval check take it around the whole pass while every UI-side service takes it too. A third acceptable shape: change IClockGuard.StartAsync/IReminderScheduler.Start to accept a Func<Func<Task>,Task> dispatcher the shell supplies (Blazor's InvokeAsync), run the pass through it, and document that contract on the interface. Add a test that runs a pass concurrently with a UI-style query on the same WakeelDb and asserts it does not throw.

findings.issue: TimeProviderMinuteTicker is registered AddSingleton (ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:67) while ReminderScheduler is AddScoped. TimeProviderMinuteTicker.Start (line 38-46) returns early when _timer is not null, silently discarding the new callback. After the first sign-out/lock-unlock (new scope, new ReminderScheduler), the singleton ticker is still bound to the OLD scheduler's RunOnceAsync, which closes over a disposed scope and a closed DbSession: every subsequent tick throws and is swallowed by the ticker's catch-all, the new scheduler never ticks, and no reminder is raised again for the rest of the process. Nothing calls IReminderScheduler.Stop() on sign-out either, so the trap is the default path, and no test covers a second Start.
findings.fix: Either register IMinuteTicker as Scoped so each session gets its own ticker, or make TimeProviderMinuteTicker.Start rebind rather than no-op: inside the lock, if _timer is not null, cancel and dispose the existing timer and CTS first, then create the new one with the new callback. Add a test asserting that Start(a) followed by Start(b) makes subsequent ticks call b, not a.

findings.issue: IBadgeService.Changed (line 124) and IClockGuard.StateChanged (ClockGuard.cs:55) are raised from thread-pool threads — BadgeService.Invalidate() is called by ReminderScheduler.RunOnceAsync (timer thread) and by QuickCaptureService, and ClockGuard.Apply raises StateChanged from its ten-minute timer callback. Neither XML doc says the handler can arrive off the renderer's synchronization context, so a B2 screen that subscribes and calls StateHasChanged directly will hit a cross-thread render failure.
findings.fix: State on both event members' XML docs that the event may be raised on a background thread and that Blazor subscribers must marshal through ComponentBase.InvokeAsync before touching component state.

findings.issue: MaxLeadMinutes (line 387) caps the meeting/appointment query horizon at max(settings default, 1440 minutes). meetings.reminder_minutes and appointments.reminder_minutes are plain ints with no upper bound, so a per-record lead time greater than one day (e.g. 2880 for a two-day heads-up) puts the meeting outside the horizon at the instant its reminder is due and the reminder is silently never raised — item 56's per-meeting override is honoured only up to 24 hours.
findings.fix: Compute the horizon from the data instead of a constant: take MAX(reminder_minutes) over the planned meetings/appointments in one scalar query (coalescing to the settings default) and use max(that, defaultMinutes) as the lead; or drop the upper bound on StartsAt and let the per-row fireAt window do the filtering. Add a test with a per-meeting reminder of 2880 minutes.

findings.issue: AttentionWindow.For (line 503) derives 'today' from utcNow.Date, while ReadTodayMeetingsAsync (line 446), NotificationService.GetPanelAsync (line 185) and ReminderScheduler's cycle reminders (line 319) all derive it from the device's LOCAL date. Between local midnight and the UTC offset (00:00–03:00 in Palestine) the attention thresholds are computed against the previous local day, so the «متأخر»/«قريب الاستحقاق» boundaries shift by a day and the W08 KPI numbers can differ from what the same data yields a few hours later.
findings.fix: In AttentionWindow.For, compute the day boundary the same way ReadTodayMeetingsAsync does: localToday = TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeFromUtc(utcNow, TimeZoneInfo.Local).Date, then convert the late/near/stale cutoffs back to UTC with TimeZoneInfo.ConvertTimeToUtc before comparing. Add a test that fixes a non-UTC zone and asserts the same row classifies identically at 01:00 and at 09:00 local.

findings.issue: CheckAsync persists all 11 cards to health_snapshots on every run and defaults persist:true (line 70, 135-150). The W12 mockup states the health center re-checks every 15 minutes, so the table grows by roughly a thousand rows a day forever with no retention, on a database the user backs up and syncs.
findings.fix: Either prune health_snapshots older than a retention window (e.g. 90 days) in the same SaveChanges, or persist a card only when its status or message differs from the newest stored snapshot for that component.

findings.issue: CheckVaultAsync's catch-all (line 247-250) returns the message «مجلد الخزنة غير موجود» for any failure, including a permissions error or an I/O failure on a folder that plainly exists. The user is told something untrue about their installation. Same shape in CheckModelsAsync (line 321-324) with «مجلد النماذج غير موجود».
findings.fix: Add distinct CoreAr strings for 'could not be inspected' (e.g. «تعذّر فحص الخزنة الآن» / «تعذّر فحص مجلد النماذج الآن») and return those from the catch blocks, keeping the 'missing' wording only for the Directory.Exists branch.

findings.issue: ReadSyncStateAsync (line 460) takes MAX(last_sync_at) over ALL devices, while HealthService.CheckSyncAsync (line 381) excludes devices with RevokedAt != null. W08's «آخر مزامنة» and W12's sync card can therefore disagree after a device is revoked, with W08 reporting a sync from hardware that is no longer trusted.
findings.fix: Add .Where(d => d.RevokedAt == null) to ReadSyncStateAsync's query so both surfaces use the same device set.

findings.issue: Money.Shekels (line 554) emits the amount as «1,234.50 ₪» (symbol trailing). In the W08 mockup the shekel sign renders leading the amount («₪ 42.50») in the phone-expense list, and since U+20AA is bidi class ET it attaches to the digit run and renders trailing in an RTL paragraph. The value also travels as AttentionItem.NumberAr into a mixed Arabic/Latin row, and nothing in Core marks it as an isolated run.
findings.fix: Confirm the intended order against design/exports/preview/light/W/W08 and, if the mockup leads with ₪, change Money.Shekels to $"₪ {agorot / 100m:#,0.00}" (InvariantCulture) — and note on AttentionItem.NumberAr's XML doc that the consumer must wrap it in <bdi> / unicode-bidi: isolate per AGREEMENT item 55.

missing_spec_items: The minute tick is never started: IReminderScheduler.Start(IMinuteTicker) and IClockGuard.StartAsync exist, are registered, and are covered by tests, but no code path in the shipped tree calls either, so the spec's «مهمة خلفية كل دقيقة» and «يشغّل ClockCheckService عند التشغيل وكل 10 دقائق» do not actually happen in the running product. The builder assigns this to the B2 screens/shell package; it must be explicitly carried forward there, and it cannot be wired safely until the high finding above is fixed.

ClockCheckTrigger.Import is defined and unit-tested but has no caller — «وعند الاستيراد» will only be satisfied when the sync package calls IClockGuard.CheckAsync(ClockCheckTrigger.Import, ...) with the imported devices' timestamps. Worth recording as a cross-package obligation.

HealthCard carries no per-card timestamp, while the W12 mockup shows «آخر فحص 10:24» on every card. Adequate in practice (HealthReport.CheckedAt applies to the whole run, since all cards run together), but the screens package must be told to use report.CheckedAt rather than expect it on the card.
notes:
VERIFICATION I RAN MYSELF. `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core` -> Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s) (TreatWarningsAsErrors is on, so warnings-as-errors is clean). `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests` -> Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 304, Skipped: 0, Total: 304, 19 s. `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop` -> Build succeeded, 0/0.

PERFORMANCE, MEASURED BY ME (not taken from the builder's report). Re-ran DailyShellPerformanceTests on this machine: `[b2-services] rows=10000 seed=1630ms attention-snapshot=46ms badges-refresh=47ms attention-counts=39ms budget=200ms`. Comfortably inside the 200 ms budget with ~4x head-room. The companion test On10kRows_TheServicesStillAgreeWithWhatWasSeeded is what makes the timing meaningful: the seeder counts exactly how many rows it made late/near/stale/pending and the services must find precisely those numbers, so a fast wrong answer fails. One caveat on the claim in AttentionService's remarks that "every query is filtered on an indexed column": the OR between a due-date predicate and an updated_at predicate cannot use a single index in SQLite, so those six queries are index-union or scan; it is fast enough at 10k and the measurement proves it, but the doc overstates the mechanism.

HOST FIDELITY, VERIFIED BY ME. Launched src/Wakeel.Desktop/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0/Wakeel.Desktop.exe with --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 and an empty temp --data-folder. /json/version answered (Edg/153.0.4234.32); /json/list reported /first-run. Captured a CDP JPEG over the websocket and looked at it: W02 renders intact in dark RTL — «مرحبًا بك في التشغيل الأول», the three-step indicator with step 2 active, «ملف الإعداد» with the drop zone, «كلمة مرور الحزمة» with the reveal eye, «فحص الحزمة», the signed-package notice, footer «الوكيل v0.21 — 16/09/2026 20:36». No server, port, internet or database wording. Host log held exactly one line ("Wakeel desktop host starting up"), no errors. Process killed; 0 Wakeel.Desktop.exe remaining.

SECURITY CHECKS REQUESTED. (1) No secrets in notifications or audit: notification titles/bodies are built only from CoreAr constants plus record titles and times; no key, password, seed, path or token reaches a row. Undo tokens are random Guids held in memory only, single-use, 2-minute expiry, never persisted. (2) The health report leaks nothing: every card message comes from CoreAr, which contains no path, no key material, no port, no server name and no engine name — notably the W12 mockup itself shows "D:\\Backups\\AlWakeel" and "(SQLCipher)", and the service deliberately does NOT, which is the correct reading of item 15. ExportText concatenates only card titles, Arabic statuses and those messages. The vault card reports a file COUNT and a mismatch count, never a file name or path. (3) Background timers do not push work onto the UI thread — WiaScannerProbe correctly offloads its blocking COM enumeration to Task.Run, and the registry/disk probes are microsecond-cheap. The hazard runs the other way (see the high finding: background timers reach into the UI's DbContext, and events fire off-thread). (4) The clock guard cannot be bypassed by dismissal: NumberingBlocked derives from the verdict alone, DismissForSession only hides the banner, an Ok check clears the dismissal, and an Import re-shows it. Numbering is blocked on Suspect as well as Bad, and OfficialNumberService.IssueAsync independently runs its own clock check and refuses on anything but Ok — so even the one fail-open path (ClockGuard's state stays Unknown/unblocked if StartAsync's first check throws) cannot actually mint a number with a bad clock. Good defence in depth; no finding.

ARABIC / RTL. All Core-emitted text lives in one file, src/Wakeel.Core/Services/CoreAr.cs, and reads as finished Arabic: no error codes, no jargon, no server/port/internet/database-engine wording (a test, NoMessageMentionsAServerAPortTheInternetOrTheDatabaseEngine, asserts this). Number agreement is handled properly (مشكلة واحدة / مشكلتان / N مشكلات / N مشكلة; يوم واحد / يومان / N أيام / N يومًا; دقيقة / دقيقتين / N دقائق). Every number goes through InvariantCulture and a test sets CurrentCulture to ar-SA and asserts no Arabic-Indic digits appear. The only Latin tokens Core emits are the product name "Word", the Office year strings and version/date strings — all of which the consuming screen must isolate with bdi. This package ships no screens and no icon-only buttons, so the tooltip rule has nothing to check here.

TEST QUALITY. The 304 tests are genuinely behavioural, not tautological. Highlights that earn their keep: a record both overdue and untouched is asserted to appear once as Late and to be absent from the Stale tab (mutual exclusivity, which is what makes the four KPI numbers add up to the list beneath them); a crafted set whose six sidebar-item badges sum to 11 is asserted to show 6 on the group header (item 26, union not sum); the item-56 lead time is tested three ways (settings default, per-meeting override, changing the default); idempotency is tested both by re-running a pass and by dismissing a reminder and re-running; the clock guard's numbering block is tested through a real OfficialNumberService issue attempt, not through the flag; quick-capture undo is tested for single-use, expiry, and the ledger lines going back. Two real bugs were found and fixed by those tests during the build (the StateChanged-every-ten-minutes comparison, and the ledger FK ordering) — both fixes are sound.

CONSUMABILITY BY THE B2 SCREENS. Mostly good: AttentionItem carries Kind + Id (navigation), Arabic kind label, title, number, party, assignee, due instant, DaysLate and the bucket; TodayMeeting/SyncState/BackupState carry ready-to-render Arabic; NotificationView carries RelativeAr and the day group; HealthCard carries a stable component id, Arabic message and an action id the UI maps to a label and route. Two gaps the screens package should be warned about: (a) the four KPI cards in the W08 mockup carry threshold-bearing subtitles («يستحق خلال 3 أيام», «بلا تحديث منذ 14 يومًا») that no service composes — the screen must build them from IAttentionService.GetThresholdsAsync; (b) W08's inner tabs are by entity type («الكل / مراسلات / مهام / التزامات»), and there is no per-kind count API — deriving them from AttentionSnapshot.NeedsActionToday would be wrong on a large database because that list is capped at 200 while Counts is uncapped, so the screen must group IAttentionService.GetAllAsync instead. Consider adding per-kind counts to AttentionSnapshot to remove the trap. Confirming/rejecting a phone expense (W08's «تأكيد/رفض مباشر», item 50) has no Core service, but that is correct: docs/build/packages/B5 assigns PhoneExpenseService explicitly, so the W08 screen has a documented cross-package dependency rather than a gap here.

OPEN ISSUES THE BUILDER RAISED, ASSESSED. The four Windows probes having no unit tests is a fair limitation (the tests project targets net10.0 and cannot reference the net10.0-windows host, and adding a project would need Wakeel.slnx); all four ran for real during my host boot, and DescribeVersion is already internal-visible for the day such a project exists. The absent unique index on notifications.source is acceptable for a single-writer database and correctly left alone rather than editing the shared migration mid-build. BadgeKeys duplicating WSidebar.Keys is unavoidable given the layering and the XML doc calls out where the equality test belongs.

VERDICT RATIONALE. Build and tests are green, the spec's service section is implemented in full and to a high standard, the performance requirement is met with room to spare, and the Arabic/security posture is genuinely careful. The verdict is 'fix' solely because of the one high finding: both background timers this package introduces write to the single shared, non-thread-safe WakeelDb, which makes a crash inevitable the moment the shell wires them as the interfaces instruct — and the medium finding that the singleton ticker silently refuses a second Start, which would kill reminders after the first lock/unlock. Both are contained in Core and fixable without touching any other package.
